title: Khronos TextureCoordinateTest -- how a uv set maps onto the image, on five plates named after the part of the image each is supposed to show

criterion.says: This model demonstrates the orientation of texture coordinates. The materials and accessors have all been named according to function. In particular, the accessor named `TopLeft_TEXCOORD_0` shows that the upper-left portion of the texture image is represented by texture coordinates ranging from roughly `0.0` to roughly `0.4`.
criterion.note: SELF-DESCRIBING AND THERE IS NO NUMERIC PROXY FOR IT. The image is a labelled template -- the words TOP LEFT, TOP RIGHT, BOTTOM LEFT, BOTTOM RIGHT are drawn into their own quadrants -- and the criterion is that each plate shows the quadrant its accessor is named after. That is a statement about WHICH GLYPHS APPEAR WHERE, and no scalar over the frame says it: a V-flip moves the same texels to different plates and changes no histogram. What the numbers below still decide is the geometry -- every plate in the right pixels -- and the picture decides the rest.

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (doc/requirements.md I.26.14). Khronos's TextureCoordinateTest is plates at several orientations, so E is in the dozens and no single roll makes them rational together.

subjects.name: TextureCoordinateTest
subjects.notes: Five plates, one back plane and four quadrant plates, over five materials of which four carry the same image through four different uv ranges and one carries no image at all. The four textured ones also carry four different non-white baseColorFactors, so the case reads the FACTOR TIMES THE TEXEL and not either alone.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of doc/requirements.md I.26.10 (src/gltf/Framing.h) applied to this subject's own bounds and to nothing else: azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.6972602252557567 m about the centre (0, 0, -0.02629531348867431), yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL, near = distance - r and far = distance + r. THE ROLL IS ZERO AND STATED: this subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so a roll would be a different draw of the same lottery rather than an exactness argument.
camera.note: The file carries no camera, so this case's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: The only illumination is Blender's factory world, and it is left where it is because configuring it would be a second thing to keep honest.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: THE ORACLE IS LOWERED, NOT THE TOLERANCE (doc/requirements.md I.26.13). The importer builds a Principled BSDF whose specular lobe survives metallicFactor 0 at IOR 1.5, so a render through it has an integral left. This arm keeps exactly what the asset is for -- its own image, its uv sets, its samplers and its four different baseColorFactors -- and replaces the closure. THE CLOSURE IS AN EMITTER AND NOT A DIFFUSE BSDF because the four plates stand in front of the back plane and shade it: at one sample per pixel a Diffuse BSDF there takes ONE cosine-weighted direction that either escapes to the world or meets a plate, so the back plane becomes a Bernoulli draw on the visible sky fraction and the case would be scoring an ambient-occlusion estimator. MEASURED at the diffuse arm: the back plane came back speckled in the reference and flat in ours, 3047 of 921600 pixels apart. An Emission at strength 1 gathers nothing, so the world as a light, the sun's disk, a light's radius and visibility leave together and what is left is baseColour(u,v)*factor. The BackPlaneMat carries no image at all and lowers the same way, to a flat emitter of its own factor -- it is not left Principled, because half a subject rendered through another closure is not a comparison.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of the emission case's acceptance. A Monte-Carlo estimator's answer depends on its seed; an emitter has no estimator, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the integral that survived.

notes: Khronos names the accessors after the part of the image they are supposed to show, so the asset states its own answer. WHAT THIS CASE CANNOT DECIDE BY A NUMBER is the last bit of a texture filter: away from one texel per pixel a path tracer's image interpolation and a rasteriser's are two definitions of one word, so the radiance residual is printed in full and the placement is what carries a threshold.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's 10 triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so.
